newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Wafabank to approve absorption of bank.
newsitem.headline: Wafabank to approve absorption of bank.

text.p: Morocco's leading Wafabank is to hold its second general assembly soon to approve the absorption of Spanish Uniban bank, a spokesman for Morocco's bankers association said on Thursday.

"Wafabank, which is expected to increase its capital by 49.2 million dirhams ($5.34 million) after a meeting in the third week of April, will definitely approve the merger-absorption of Uniban," the spokesman told Reuters.
Uniban extraordinary assembly has already approved the absorption on February 26, 1997, the spokesman said.
Wafabank bought 100 percent of Uniban or more than 2.46 million shares priced at about $28 million, he said.
Wafabank offered one share in exchange for five shares of Uniban despite some opposition from minority shareholders, a Casablanca-based market analyst said.
The minority group which holds around 7.0 percent of Uniban stock continues to dispute the takeover before a Casablanca court, the analyst said.
Wafabank recently said it made a net profit of 242 million dirhams ($25.7 million) in calendar year 1996, up 20 percent on the 201 million dirhams of the previous year.
It said deposits totalled 13.8 billion dirhams, an increase of 14.25 percent over the previous period, lifting the bank's market share to 9.8 percent from nine percent.
Loans to clients rose just over 16 percent to 11.1 billion dirhams, while its mutual funds raised 997 million dirhams, 37 percent of the market.

A private local group owns 50.4 percent of Wafabank. Another 10.4 percent, previously held by French Groupe Suez, was ceded last July to Indosuez Bank group. The remaining 39.2 percent of Wafabank's equity is publicly owned.
Uniban showed a 27.2 million dirhams loss in 1995 due mainly to provisions for non-performing debt, the bank said. No updated figures for 1996 were immediately available.
The dissolution of Uniban and its delisting from the Casablanca stock market after its merger with Wafabank is expected by end of June 1997, a bourse official said.
